clue.text: A vote on the other side

blocks.note: taken as written
a voter marks the ballot paper with a cross

explanation.surface: Someone casts a ballot for the opposing party.
explanation.walkthrough: A vote reads as a single phrase, but the A stands alone and the vote is the mark made on a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something situated over the way, beyond a road or river, lies across from the speaker, a plain locational synonym.

clue.text: Down i Beginning to take a chance with the letters

blocks.note: scan debris: the printed column heading and clue number, not part of the clue
alpha, the first Greek letter, means the beginning, as in alpha and omega
to bet is to gamble, taking a chance

explanation.surface: A beginner gambles on learning to read and write.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening Down i is the scanned column heading and clue number, not part of the clue; the clue proper starts at Beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: The full ordered set of characters used to write a language is its alphabet, so the letters collectively name it.

clue.text: Scoffing at a guard

definitions.note: a noun phrase; the answer as a noun is the barrier itself

blocks.note: first meaning: to rail at someone is to complain bitterly or mock them
second meaning: a fence of bars that guards an edge or stair

explanation.surface: Someone jeers at a sentry on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes guard a person being mocked; in the second sense it is a protective barrier of bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Railing at someone is reproaching or mocking them, and a railing is also a barrier of bars protecting an edge.

clue.text: Hush - outbreak of measles, and not a modest one

definitions.note: describes such a person; the answer is the adjective

indicators.note: an outbreak scatters things, so the word that follows breaks out of its usual order

blocks.note: sh is the sound made to call for quiet
the letters of measles rearranged

explanation.surface: A call for quiet over a measles outbreak, by someone who is far from modest.
explanation.walkthrough: Outbreak of measles sounds like an epidemic, but it is the anagram signal working on the disease's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no sense of modesty or embarrassment is shameless; the clue describes such a person rather than giving a synonym.

clue.text: Forward a reasonable claim

definitions.note: a phrase defining the answer split as I'M MODEST

blocks.note: first meaning: forward as an adjective means bold or presumptuous
second meaning: split after its second letter, the answer becomes the claim ..., modest meaning reasonable in demands

explanation.surface: Putting forward a fair request.
explanation.walkthrough: Forward reads as a verb to put a claim forward; it is the adjective for bold. The joke is that saying you are modest is itself boastful.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward person is pushy and bold, lacking the reserve of modesty, so the adjective matches exactly.

clue.text: Walter's lot, more adaptable as coast-guards

indicators.note: something adaptable can be reshaped, so these letters are free to take a new order

blocks.note: the letters of Walter's, lot and more taken together

explanation.surface: Walter and his crew, being flexible, are drafted in as coastguards.
explanation.walkthrough: Martello towers are the small round forts built along the English coast against a Napoleonic invasion.
explanation.definitionFit: These round defensive forts were built along British coasts to guard against invasion, so they were literally guards of the coast.

clue.text: Admitted being had

definitions.note: a participle phrase; the answer is a past participle

blocks.note: first meaning: to own up to something is to admit it
second meaning: something possessed is had by its possessor

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they were tricked.
explanation.walkthrough: Being had suggests being fooled; here it simply means being possessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Owned up means confessed, and a thing that is owned is held as a possession by someone.

clue.text: Disposition of the army, see - hence chaos about

indicators.note: chaos is utter disorder, so the word before it is thrown out of order
about means surrounding, so the jumbled word goes round the other piece

blocks.note: the letters of hence rearranged
lo is the old word for look or see

explanation.surface: A general surveys his scattered troops and finds them in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: LO, as in lo and behold, is a crossword stock for see.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a stepped formation of troops, a particular arrangement or disposition of military units.

clue.text: Drawing to wound

blocks.note: taken as written
to wing someone is to wound them, especially in the arm

explanation.surface: Sketching something to hurt someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Drawing suggests art; here it means pulling along, as a tug does.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle hauling another behind it on a rope is drawing it, an established sense of pulling along.

clue.text: Sterne's journeyman

blocks.note: surface reading: a skilled craftsman employed by someone named Sterne
setter's reading: the man making the journey in Laurence Sterne's novel A Sentimental Journey

explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne wrote A Sentimental Journey through France and Italy in 1768; its hero, Yorick, is the traveller meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given to tender feelings is a sentimentalist, and the narrator of Sterne's sentimental journey is the archetype of one.

clue.text: Soldier about to return with old raider

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word for about is read backwards

blocks.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A soldier is about to come home with a former marauder.
explanation.walkthrough: About to return reads as soon going home; it splits into the word for about and the instruction to reverse it.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was an armed private ship, or its captain, licensed to attack enemy shipping, a raider of former times.

clue.text: Not at all specialised skill, say

indicators.note: say asks for the words to be spoken, so what counts is how they sound

blocks.note: know-how is practical expertise

explanation.surface: Someone denies having any particular expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: Nohow is a dialect or informal adverb meaning in no way whatsoever, so it replaces not at all.

clue.text: Soldiers, with a drunk around, getting food

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the drunk wraps round the soldiers

blocks.note: a plus lit, slang for drunk
men are soldiers, as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Troops surround a drunk while being fed.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk looks like a noun for a person; it is a plus an adjective meaning intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for nourishment or sustenance, anything that feeds, related to alimentary.

clue.text: Phantom hero in eternity

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

blocks.note: an idol is a person hero-worshipped
an eon is an immeasurably long age

explanation.surface: A ghostly hero lives on forever.
explanation.definitionFit: An eidolon is an idealised image or spectral apparition, from the Greek for image, so a ghost or apparition.

clue.text: Bird makes a dog lose its head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the dog breed is dropped

blocks.note: a beagle is a breed of hunting dog

explanation.surface: A bird of prey frightens a dog into panic.
explanation.walkthrough: Lose its head suggests panic; here it removes the first letter of the breed.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a large bird of prey, a straightforward example of the general category.

clue.text: Hit back about one lad making curses

indicators.note: back means the word for hit is read in the opposite direction
about means surrounding, so the reversed word goes round the following pieces

blocks.note: to slam is to hit hard
I is the Roman numeral one
a son is a boy or lad

explanation.surface: Someone retaliates against a boy, swearing as they do.
explanation.walkthrough: Hit back reads as retaliate; it is the word for hit turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Malison is an archaic word for a curse, the opposite of benison, so the plural matches curses.

clue.text: Master Pistol, a jocularly familiar lad

blocks.note: first meaning: Master is the title of a boy, a son, and a pistol is a firearm, so a young boy of the weapon
second meaning: a teasing, affectionate term for a fellow

explanation.surface: A boy named Pistol is introduced in a chummy way.
explanation.walkthrough: Master Pistol looks like a Shakespearean name; it is read literally as a boy belonging to a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: The expression is an affectionate or mildly exasperated form of address for a man or boy, used jokingly between friends.

clue.text: Bust made descriptively impossible

blocks.note: first meaning: bust means bankrupt, reduced to poverty
second meaning: a sight that beggars description cannot be described

explanation.surface: A sculpted bust so remarkable that it cannot be described.
explanation.walkthrough: Bust suggests a sculpture; it is the informal word for financially ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reduced to poverty has been beggared, and the idiom beggar description means to defy any attempt at words.

clue.text: Nests are made into silky stuff

indicators.note: made into says the words are reworked into something new

blocks.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: Birds' nests are being lined with soft fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarsenet is a fine soft silk fabric used for linings, so it is a silky material or stuff.

clue.text: Diana going Greek

blocks.note: surface reading: a woman named Diana adopting Greek ways or travelling to Greece
setter's reading: the Roman goddess Diana under her Greek name

explanation.walkthrough: Diana, the Roman huntress goddess, was identified with a Greek goddess of hunting and the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman Diana corresponds to the Greek huntress and moon goddess, twin sister of Apollo, so translating her into Greek gives this name.

clue.text: Jab, let's say, and pester in return

indicators.note: in return means turned back, so the two pieces are read from the end

blocks.note: eg, for example, is what let's say introduces
to dun is to pester for payment of a debt

explanation.surface: Someone pokes another and nags them back.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a light push with the elbow, a gentle jab to attract attention.

clue.text: Girl rising - leave a drop

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, from the bottom

blocks.note: bird is British slang for a girl or young woman
to let someone do something is to leave them to it

explanation.surface: A girl gets up and leaves a drip behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A driblet is a tiny quantity, especially a small drop of liquid, related to dribble.

clue.text: Direction briefly repeated with River Festival

blocks.note: east is a compass direction
the same direction again in its short form
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A short repeated direction leads to a river festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass point is given twice, once in full and once as its single-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the major Christian feast celebrating the Resurrection, a festival of the church year.

clue.text: As a feeler, before noon - no Scotch!

blocks.note: ante is Latin for before
N is the abbreviation for noon
na is the Scots word for no

explanation.surface: Someone sounding things out in the morning, refusing whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch suggests whisky; here it means in Scots dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's antenna is its sensory feeler, used to touch and smell its surroundings.

clue.text: For the moment there's nobody round about

definitions.note: the answer is used in the phrase for the nonce, which means this

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the word for nobody goes round the abbreviation for about

blocks.note: none means not one person
c is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: For now, nobody is anywhere nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The nonce is the present occasion, so for the nonce is an old idiom meaning temporarily, for the time being.

clue.text: Speed around a short distance, going easily

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for speed goes round the short distance

blocks.note: to wing is to fly or travel swiftly
a plus ft, the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: Racing round a short track before cruising gently.
explanation.walkthrough: A short distance suggests a little way; it means the abbreviated unit, a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Wafting describes drifting lightly through the air, like a scent, moving gently and effortlessly.

clue.text: Man, briefly, dealing with a misanthrope

blocks.note: Tim is the short form of the man's name Timothy
on means concerning or dealing with, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A short man is dealing with someone who hates people.
explanation.walkthrough: Man, briefly suggests an abbreviation like IOM; it is a shortened man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Timon of Athens is the title figure who turns against all humanity, the classic literary hater of mankind.

clue.text: Disorderly - not even abnormal!

blocks.note: first meaning: lacking order or pattern
second meaning: contrary to the usual rule or norm

explanation.surface: An exclamation about something chaotic and not even normal.
explanation.walkthrough: Not even is itself a third sense, uneven, so all three phrases describe the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular describes what is out of order, uneven in shape or spacing, and contrary to rule or normal practice.

clue.text: Particular point with honours

definitions.note: a verb, matching the answer read as a verb

blocks.note: first meaning: a respect is a detail or aspect
second meaning: to respect someone is to hold them in high regard

explanation.surface: Making a specific point and adding awards.
explanation.definitionFit: A respect is an aspect or particular detail, and to respect someone is to esteem them, so respects means honours.

clue.text: How to stand a soccer team

definitions.note: the answer completes the saying united we stand

blocks.note: first meaning: the proverb says ... we stand, divided we fall
second meaning: many football clubs are called ..., such as Manchester ...

explanation.surface: Advice on how to support your football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that people stand together when joined, and United is the stock name of numerous football clubs.
